name: Cross-origin isolation (SharedArrayBuffer, COOP, COEP)
plain: A site can opt into an isolated mode that unlocks SharedArrayBuffer, precise timers and Wasm threads.
meaning: Isolation trades openness (no cross-origin popups or unmarked embeds) for power. Sites with it get memory sharing and 5 microsecond timers, which are also better side channel tools.

web.api: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin; Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp or credentialless; self.crossOriginIsolated

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Embedded frames need CORP or CORS (require-corp) or credentialless mode
steps: Server sends COOP and COEP headers
SharedArrayBuffer and fine timers become available

limits.headline: Can switch on a locked down mode that unlocks fast shared memory for the page
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the site loads with the right security headers set.
can: Share memory between background threads for heavy apps like games and editors
Run the page's own code with very precise timers
Start multi threaded compiled code inside the page
cannot: Open popups that stay linked to other sites while isolation is on
Load embedded videos, ads or widgets that are not marked to allow it
Turn itself on without the site's own server sending the right headers
See anything in other tabs or other sites
limits.differs: Works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, including on iPhone and Android.

story.what_it_is: A site can switch on a locked down mode that unlocks very fast, shared memory tricks.

marketing.name: Cross-origin isolation
marketing.pitch: Chrome's web.dev guide says isolation unlocks powerful features like SharedArrayBuffer and high precision timers, in exchange for stricter rules about embeds.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. A big web app just runs smoother, but some embedded widgets, like a video or ad frame, may refuse to load until their owners add the right labels.
story.for_makers: Makers flip this on to get shared memory and multi threaded compiled code, which game engines and heavy editors need. The cost is that every third party embed on the page must opt in too, which is a real project for ad heavy sites.

use_cases.example: A Unity or Unreal game exported to the browser uses several worker threads at once, which only works when the page is isolated.
A web video editor trims and renders clips using many CPU threads so the preview stays smooth.
Spreadsheets and CAD tools in the browser share one big block of memory between workers to crunch numbers faster.
An in browser coding sandbox runs a whole Node style environment and needs shared memory to do it.
Security teams use isolation to make sure that a page cannot be read by other sites' scripts, a defence against Spectre style attacks.
Ad networks must retag their frames and scripts so a publisher can turn isolation on without breaking ad slots.

technical_bounds: COEP require-corp: every subresource needs CORP or CORS; credentialless mode available in Chrome 96 and Firefox 119
COOP same-origin severs window.opener to cross-origin popups (breaks OAuth popups unless same-origin-allow-popups)
Isolated pages get performance.now at 5 microsecond resolution (Chrome) instead of 100 microseconds
Chrome on Android got SharedArrayBuffer under the same rule in 92

abuse: Fast timer side channels (Spectre style) if isolation fails
